article_title: Nvidia Introduces a 64GB DGX Spark Starting at $4,999 as the 128GB Model's Price Rises to $6,950

content_preview.title: Nvidia Introduces a 64GB DGX Spark Starting at $4,999 as the 128GB Model's Price Rises to $6,950
content_preview.summary: Nvidia's 64GB DGX Spark ships October 23 from partners from $4,999, with unchanged bandwidth and clustering, while the 128GB model's price rose to $6,950 amid a memory shortage.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Nvidia is adding a lower-memory configuration of its DGX Spark desktop AI system. According to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/systems/2026/10/02/nvidia-debuts-4999-dgx-spark-with-half-the-ram-and-storage-amid-memory-crunch/5300622), the new GB10-based systems have half the memory and storage of the existing model, are sold exclusively through hardware partners including Acer, Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, HP, and MSI, and are expected to retail for around $4,999. The same report...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News structure (Overview, What We Know, Why the Smaller Configuration, Competition, What We Don't Know), 658 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Appropriate technical depth; internal link /article/2026-09/09-nvidia-releases-personal-ai-router-... resolves to an existing published article.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three snapshots from disk (source-0 The Register, source-1 blogs.nvidia.com, source-2 Tom's Hardware), decompressed with gzip and text-extracted. All manifests show status 200 and suspicious_patterns null for each source. All three domains (theregister.com, blogs.nvidia.com, tomshardware.com) are in config/source_allowlist.txt. source-0 (The Register): confirms 64GB model offered exclusively through partners 'including Acer, Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, HP, and MSI' and 'expected to retail for around $4,999'; 'Nvidia jacked the price of its 128 GB DGX Spark on Friday to $6,950 - an increase of nearly 75 percent from this time last year' (rise already in effect, stated by The Register; Tom's Hardware corroborates with 'Nvidia's adjusted MSRP'); 'memory bandwidth remains unchanged at 273 GB/s' and the inference that lower-capacity LPDDR5x modules are used; 20-core MediaTek Arm CPU; ConnectX-7 clustering 'up to 4x GB10-based devices at 200 Gbps a piece'; new software tools 'later this month' for cluster config and inference deployments, previously needing CLI tinkering with vLLM/TensorRT-LLM; 64GB less suited to fine tuning and Nvidia argues 26-35B models such as Qwen 3.8 27B suffice; AMD 'Gorgon Halo' SoCs with ~32 GB to 192 GB for the top Ryzen AI Max+ 495 SKUs, systems currently retail for less than the 128 GB DGX Spark, and The Register's own testing shows GB10 GPU 'substantially higher performance for AI tasks'. source-1 (Nvidia blog): 'DGX Spark 64GB is available from Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI on Friday, Oct. 23, starting at $4,999'; keeps GB10, DGX OS, full AI software stack 'same as the 128GB model'; 'supports up to 100-billion-parameter models'; 'two units can connect directly with a QSFP cable'; 'In NVIDIA's Qwen 3.8 27B test, two clustered 64 GB systems delivered up to 1.7x performance'; Sync Cluster Assistant 'detects connected units, validates device configuration and configures the ConnectX-7 network'; Sync Model Launcher 'coming at the end of the month' to download and launch Qwen3.8 27B on a single system or cluster; Ollama, vLLM, PyTorch with CUDA supported out of the box. source-2 (Tom's Hardware): the snapshot is complete, not truncated (it contains the full article text, ending with the clustering/273 GB/s paragraph and related-article links). Confirms '64GB GB10 systems from Acer, Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, HP, and MSI are slated to start at $4999 when they launch on October 23', 'they might not stay there for long', 'roughly $7000 to $9000' for an in-stock 128GB system 'far above even Nvidia's adjusted MSRP', unchanged 273 GB/s bandwidth, same ConnectX 7 NIC enabling clustering, same 20-core Arm CPU, dense models like Qwen 3.8 27B fit within 32GB 'albeit with limited context', and the RAM-price rationale. Every Tom's Hardware attribution in the article traces to text present in the snapshot.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All prices ($4,999; $6,950), 64GB figure, October 23 date, 273 GB/s bandwidth, two-unit clustering (Nvidia) and up-to-4-device clustering (The Register), and the AMD competition claim trace to the cited sources and are attributed to the right outlet. The 128GB price rise is attributed to The Register, is stated as already in effect (done 'on Friday', i.e. Oct 2) and gives the old-price context correctly as nearly 75% above a year earlier. Partners named (Acer, Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, HP, MSI) match all three sources exactly; none invented. The 'new software tooling' claim matches Nvidia's text (Sync Cluster Assistant; Sync Model Launcher at end of month) and The Register's framing. The sole performance figure (1.7x, Qwen 3.8 27B clustering) is explicitly labeled as Nvidia's own test, and the AMD performance remark is attributed to The Register's testing. Minor imprecision, non-material: the article calls the Ryzen AI Max+ 495 a 'line' with 32-192 GB capacities, whereas The Register attributes those capacities to the Gorgon Halo SoCs with the 495 as the top SKU; the Nvidia blog's 'Coming this month' availability vs. the specific Oct. 23 date is correctly sourced to Nvidia's 'Get Started' section. No fabricated quotes (no direct quotations used).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; vendor claims attributed to Nvidia, no editorializing, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald article covers the DGX Spark 64GB configuration or the 128GB price increase. The only related article (Nvidia Personal AI Router, 2026-09) is a different story and is referenced as context. New topic.
recommendations: Optionally name the Gorgon Halo SoC family when describing AMD's Ryzen AI Max+ 495 competition, matching The Register's wording.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced, correctly attributed News article. Headline, summary and lead are each backed by cited sources. Approved without corrections.
